verdict.observations: Raster toolbar reads 56% and shows the complete fit-like network, while its paired public record declares 100% and a 100% camera. The actual raster itself is clean and all five routes are visible, but it cannot certify the declared 100% local view.

Clear post-generation raster at 56% shows all five nodes and five routes with legible node labels, clean orthogonal routing, visible arrowheads, no body penetration, and no visible producer crossing. Port names are small at this overview scale.

Actual 56% fit raster shows all five nodes and five arrows. Orthogonal routes terminate at visible port circles; no body penetration or distinct-producer crossing is visible. Output input remains selected, which adds a blue focus outline but does not obscure the route.
A generated-model modal covers the canvas and applies a dim/blur overlay; the route layout cannot be visually reviewed from this raster.

Raster toolbar reads 100% and crops away both input nodes and the Output node, while the paired public record declares 56%. The enlarged Add/Concat junction is legible and shows separated a/b arrivals, but the full network cannot be judged.

Actual 56% reopened raster shows the complete five-node/five-edge network. Add is selected; its outline does not cover any edge. Routes remain orthogonal, with clean port endpoints and no visible body penetration or crossing.
Add moved down; routes remain attached and readable, with no visible crossing or body penetration.
Add moved left; input routes and Add→Concat route visibly reroute cleanly. No body penetration or crossing is visible. Undo control is focused in this frame.
Add moved right to the declared visible position; all five routes visibly follow it with orthogonal bends, intact endpoints, and no body penetration/crossing.
Add moved up; the two input routes and output route remain attached through orthogonal segments. No visible crossing or node-body penetration.
All five nodes and five routes remain visible after down pan; orthogonal routing and arrow endpoints stay intact with no visible crossings or body penetration.

globalPixelFindings.clear56PercentFrames: All clear full-network 56% frames reviewed (fit, reopened, and four node moves) show orthogonal routes, visible arrowheads at ports, no route entering a node body, and no visible distinct-producer crossing.
globalPixelFindings.fanout: A→Concat.b uses a long exterior multi-bend route around the graph; bends are 90-degree and avoid node bodies, but its length is a remaining publication-aesthetic concern.
globalPixelFindings.movement: Right/left/up/down 16-unit Add moves visibly preserve attachment and routing. Pixel evidence covers the four JPEG frames; redo/base-restored have no JPEG and are therefore DOM-only for this review.
globalPixelFindings.pan: Vertical pan frames retain the full network. Horizontal pan frames intentionally clip endpoint nodes at canvas boundaries, so only visible segments are judged.
globalPixelFindings.portLegibility: Node names are readable in the 56% overview, but the small port names are not comfortable at that scale. Enlarged central Add/Concat raster makes them easier to distinguish, while its state-pair mismatch remains open.

knownMismatchesAndLimits: merge-100-local.jpg displays 56% in pixels while paired public state declares 100%; the raster cannot certify a 100% local view.
merge-reopened-settled.jpg displays 100% in pixels while paired public state declares 56%; it is a central crop and does not show the complete graph.
merge-final-fit.jpg is a dimmed/blurred generated-model modal, so it is not a route-layout proof.
JPEG observations are pixel evidence only; DOM path geometry cannot override a raster mismatch or crop.

remainingConcerns: Fix screenshot/state pairing for the 100% local and reopened-settled cases before using them as evidence.
